neighbours.label: Pronoun or negation inside prose about vulnerable people's access to care, benefits or services ('the care they need', 'who do not qualify'); the same structures about other subjects stay quiet
fire: Many disabled veterans still wait for the home care they were promised.
Refugee children seldom receive the counselling they need after arriving.
Uninsured adults who do not have a doctor often go to the emergency room.
Single mothers on welfare often lose the childcare subsidies they depend on.
Seniors who may not read English struggle to claim the pensions they have earned.
People with mental illness are frequently denied the treatment they seek.
Homeless teenagers do not always know about the shelter services they can use.
A woman leaving an abusive home may not get the legal aid she needs.
quiet: Many retired pilots still wait for the old planes they were promised.
Rival chess clubs seldom receive the trophies they want after a match.
Old bicycles that do not have a chain often go to the scrapyard.
Young sailors on leave often lose the playing cards they carry.
Disabled veterans in the county received home care from a local charity.
Uninsured adults visit the emergency room at twice the average rate.
Refugee children attended counselling sessions at the new community centre.
Homeless teenagers used the downtown shelter during the winter months.
